conflict_topics: Participation in the shared dinner rota during Agent D's vegetarian month (Purattasi)
Whether the rota's purpose requires everyone to share the same single cooked meal versus sitting together while some cook separate food
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation reads like a natural roommate negotiation: announcements, expression of constraint, offers of solutions, and an explicit confirmation.
Key problem framed both practically (who can cook vegetarian) and symbolically (value of sharing one person's meal).
Proposals were concrete (swap days, find a recipe, cook separate food) and led to a concrete agreement rather than vague promises.
evaluation.final_reason: The group agreed to a concrete swap of rota nights so that Agent D's vegetarian month is accommodated without forcing non-vegetarian cooks to learn new recipes. Agent A accepted the swap: "But swapping days works for me." Agent B agreed to it: "Yeah, I don't mind. It's fine." Agent D also confirmed the arrangement in the next round. This is a compromise: A and B adjusted their scheduled nights to accommodate D's dietary requirement.
position_change_notes: Agent A: initially said their dishes contain meat and hesitated about new recipes; then accepted swapping days: "But swapping days works for me."
Agent B: initially said they can eat vegetarian and then proactively offered to swap days: "Or I can swap my day with you for this month." B later confirmed agreement: "Yeah, I don't mind."
Agent D: announced the dietary restriction, proposed cooking separate food as an accommodation, and later confirmed the final swap arrangement: "Okay, that works for me."
Agent C: expressed willingness to eat vegetarian but kept their existing cooking commitment unchanged; they did not change position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D announced a change: "It's the month of Purattasi... I'm vegetarian for the whole month." Agent A immediately queried the change: "What do you mean, not the usual way?" — a new incompatibility with the existing rota was introduced but not yet disputed.

Agent A stated a practical inability to comply with the vegetarian requirement: "But all the dishes I know how to make have meat in them." Agent B indicated willingness to eat vegetarian. This made the practical incompatibility concrete (who will cook/what will be eaten).

Agent C said they can eat vegetarian but kept the expectation of "still only cooking one night a week." Agent D offered an accommodation: "For anyone who can't make a vegetarian dish, on your night Agent A, I can just cook my own food. You all can eat what you normally eat." The practical problem was addressed but a normative issue (shared single meal) remained unsettled.

Agent A raised a value-based objection: "But the whole point was for all of us to eat together." Agent D responded that they can still eat together despite separate cooking: "I'll cook my food, and we can still all eat together at the table." This exposed a clear disagreement about whether separate cooking preserves the rota's purpose.

Agent A reiterated the symbolic point: "It's not really the same... The point is sharing the meal that one person has cooked for everyone." Agent B proposed practical solutions: "Why don't we find you an easy vegetarian recipe? Or I can swap my day with you for this month." A concrete compromise was offered, reducing but not yet eliminating the conflict.

Agent A accepted a compromise: "But swapping days works for me. Are you sure you don't mind?" Agent B confirmed: "Yeah, I don't mind. It's fine." The parties with incompatible demands agreed on a concrete arrangement (A and B will swap their cooking days for the month), settling the substantive conflict.

Participants affirmed the previously agreed arrangement: Agent D: "Okay, that works for me. Thanks for sorting that out." Agent A: "Okay, great. So we'll just swap for the month then." No substantive disagreement remained.
No public speech or observable action recorded; the swap had already been confirmed in prior rounds.

substantive_insights: The disagreement combined a practical constraint (some cooks only know meat dishes) with a symbolic expectation (the rota's point is to share one person's meal).
Low-cost scheduling swaps are an effective compromise for temporary dietary constraints among cohabitants.
Agent D offered an accommodation (cooking separate food) that addressed logistics but did not satisfy the symbolic sharing concern, which required a schedule change to resolve.
